answer: To deter Sybil attacks across a walnut grove, shale ridge, and yarrow meadow, agents authenticate peers via seismic time-of-flight ranging. Nodes emit subterranean acoustic pulses, verifying physical separation through acoustic arrival delays. An attacker cannot fabricate distinct locations without deploying discrete geophones per identity, imposing non-virtualizable hardware and deployment costs. However, moisture shifts alter rock acoustic velocity, triggering false attestation rejections.
